note: Hand-curated research for a Geographica episode about the Danube. Claims are cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary). The river is drawn as a route through cities on its banks, not traced from map data; the city points are approximate. Moldova and Ukraine are flagged countries in the map data (Transnistria, Crimea and others; none shown), so the episode needs the borders review before release.

claims.text: In the 21st century the Danube connects ten European countries, running through their territories or marking a border.
The Danube originates in Germany and flows through or borders Austria, Slovakia, Hungary, Croatia, Serbia, Romania, Bulgaria, Moldova and Ukraine.
It passes through four capital cities: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade.
The Danube is the second-longest river in Europe after the Volga; it flows southeast for about 2,850 km.
It originates in the town of Donaueschingen, in the Black Forest of Germany, at the confluence of the Brigach and Breg.
It empties into the Black Sea through the Danube Delta in Romania and Ukraine.

delta.note: The Danube Delta, at the Black Sea.
